Commentary.Commentary: 265 does not look a total as big as the high 300s but this pitch is certainly not easy to bat on. The new ball will move around the cracks will make the ball turn. But the pitch seems to have eased out a touch. Join us back at 1345 local (0815 GMT).

A better day for the Irish bowlers but they will feel they let things slip a bit. They could have restricted the Afghans to a much smaller total but could not contain in the death overs. They went for as many as 91 in the last 10, with 54 coming off the final 5. Chase started off well, with a couple of wickets upfront but could not maintain his consistency. Tim Murtagh was the most economical of the seamers and would have been the best overall, but for his last over which went for 21. Still, he finished decently with 2/49. Dockrell held things tight in the middle with 1/40 in 10 overs while Stirling was under-bowled today. Even McBrine, who had figures of 7-1-26-1, did not get a second chance.

Shafiqullah Shafaq and Dawlat Zadran came together and proved why Afghanistan's batting is so deep. The duo added 71 from just 42 balls, with Shafaq racing to a 28-ball 50. Zadran did his bit, giving strike to Shafaq as much as possible. This is the first time that NUMBERS 7,8 AND 9 have scored half centuries in the same ODI innings.

Naib and Khan batted sensibly, taking quick singles but attacking as well. Slowly, the runs started to come at a greater speed and then, without Ireland realizing, the attack started. Rashid Khan was particularly severe, scoring a half century at more than run-a-ball. The visitors came back though, removing both batsmen in the 43rd over but they had more problems in store.

With the ball seaming around, Ireland struck early today. Peter Chase removed both the openers and then the other bowlers came to the party. They had the Afghans on the mat, at 97/6 but then a 96-run stand between Naib and Rashid Khan stalled things.

Magnificent batting display from Afghanistan today again. It was a different scenario, with wickets going early upfront, but the lower order hung around. Half centuries from Gulbadin Naib, Rashid Khan and Shafiqullah Shafaq have helped their side post a commanding total under these conditions.

The batsman has pushed it to the cover region.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.

Full and wide outside off, Stanikzai slashes but misses. Chase is lucky that is not wided. Replays show that the ball went past the wide guideline. 5 runs and a wicket from the over, Chase has figures of 3-0-12-2!
A second slip comes in place.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
ASGHAR STANIKZAI walks in at number 4, replacing Shahzad.

OUT! Edged and taken! Full and outside off, Shahzad pushes inside the line and gets a thick outside edge. The ball goes towards first lip where Gary Wilson takes it nicely to his right. Chase has gone for runs, but he has picked up wickets as well. In fact, he is making a comeback of sorts.
A short ball around off, MS looks to pull but mistimes it back to the bowler.
Fuller and straighter, defended with a straight bat.
WIDE. NUMBER 6 from Chase. He has bowled an extra over in itself. Bowls this full and wide outside off, Mohammad lets it go.
FOUR! BANG! A short ball around off, Shahzad rocks back and heaves it through mid-wicket for a boundary! Moves to 11 from 12 balls with his second boundary.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
Full and outside off, worked wide of mid on for a single.
Landed around off, pushed towards cover.
Full and outside off, Rahmat leans and drives it through the covers. But Stuart Thompson dives to his right and parries it towards mid off.
Full and outside off, this time, it is defended well towards the off side.
Full and straight, Shah gets squared up a touch and defends unconvincingly.

A lovely ball to end the over. Keeps this full and outside off, Mohammad comes forward to work this to the leg side but the ball moves away to take the outside edge towards point. Just 2 runs and a wicket from the over. Good comeback from Chase after an indifferent opening over.
A short ball, down the leg side, nudged fine towards fine leg for a single to get off the mark.
WIDE. Slants this down the leg side, Shah is not able to get it away. Seems like Chase is chasing for pace. But is not able to control his line.
RAHMAT SHAH walks in at number 3, replacing Noor Ali.

OUT! CAUGHT! Chase strikes! Noor Ali was struggling and has been dismissed. Full and wide outside off, Zadran looks to drive on the rise, does not get to the pitch of the ball and fails to keep it down. The ball flies towards cover where George Dockrell dives forward and takes a sharp catch. An early breakthrough for the visiting side.
Lovely ball. Lands this outside off, cuts it back sharply, Zadran is cut into two as the ball stays low as well.
Around off, coming in, worked towards short mid-wicket.
Full and wide outside off, Noor Ali plays a loose cover drive without moving his feet and misses.
Outside off, tapped towards third man for a single to get off the mark.
Good line, full and outside off, swinging away, Noor Ali comes forward and shoulders arms.
Deep square leg comes in while fine leg drops back.
Another short delivery, closer to the off stump, pulled towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Fuller in length, once again Mohammad plays inside the line and pushes it towards cover.
FOUR! AUDACIOUS! Slightly wide outside off, short in length, Shahzad does not spare it, backs away a touch and smashes it behind point for a boundary!
On a good length around off, Shahzad gets back in his crease and defends.
TIM MURTAGH to bowl with the second new ball.
Fuller in length, swinging in, Noor Ali works it towards short mid-wicket. End of a 10-ball opening over. Chase seems to be continuing from where he left in the previous game.
Outside off, played in front of covers for a quick single. Shahzad is off the mark.
Good point by Chetan Sharma on air. He says that Ireland bowlers do not warm up in the nets before the game. Had Chase done that, he would not have bowled so many wides.
Excellent bowling. Lands this on a good length around off, MS looks to defend but the ball bounces steeply and goes off the leading edge. Does not carry to the bowler.
FOURTH WIDE OF THE OVER. This is just the first over. Another one slanting down the leg side, Mohammad lets it go.
Flat-footed. On a good length outside off, Shahzad stays rooted in his crease and flays at it, only to miss. Very loose.
Finally gets the inswinger correct, puts it on a better line, on a good length outside off, shouldered arms to.
HAT-TRICK OF WIDES. A slower ball, but down the leg side, MS cannot get this one away either. Seems like he is struggling when trying to bowl the inswinger.
ANOTHER WIDE. Exploring both sides of the pitch. This is full and wide outside off, Mohammad looks to thrash this but misses.

WIDE. Unable to control the movement there. Chase lands this around leg stump and then sprays it further wide down the leg side. Shahzad still goes for the pull but misses. Niall O'Brien covers good ground to his left to collect.
Slightly short of a length outside off, bit of away moment, played towards point.

The players are out in the middle. Mohammad Shahzad and Noor Ali Zadran are the openers for Afghanistan. It will be PETER CHASE to start off proceedings. Went for a plenty in the last match. He will bowl to Shahzad first up. Here we go...
TEAM CHANGES - Both teams are unchanged from the previous ODI. That is a little surprising. One would have expected Peter Chase to sit on the bench today.

WILLIAM PORTERFIELD agrees that the pitch indeed looks different. He says Ireland expect used pitches to be played as matches are at the same venue. Rues the inability to capitalize on platforms in the previous games and stresses that the aim is to continue playing good cricket and opes to get across the line today. Is confident about winning this series as well as on the previous two series that they played, Ireland beat Afghanistan in each.

ASGHAR STANIKZAI says that the wicket looks a bit different today and could support spin in the second innings. Agrees that the Afghan batsmen are in very good form and praises the openers for setting a platform consistently. Hopes to win the series today itself and set a target in excess of 250.
TOSS - Another victory in this department for Stanikzai. Heads is the call from Porterfield but it comes down as Tails. AFGHANISTAN ELECT TO BAT FIRST AGAIN.

PITCH REPORT - It looks a different wicket today. There are some cracks visible which should help the spinners. There is a little bit of grass covering to bind the surface. So no question other than to win the toss and bat first. There is a little bit of cloud cover but that should not hep the seamers much.
WEATHER - It is an overcast morning in Noida today. However, there is no threat of rain.

3 T20Is gone, two ODIs have followed and we are yet to see a result which is not similar to the previous one. Almost in every game, one sees the Afghan side in trouble, only to later watch them bounce back. While this reinforces the quality of the home side, what it also tells us is the lack of confidence and self-belief in the Irish. A loss today will mean that this series is also gone for the Men in Green. Can they spark a turnaround? Hello and a warm welcome to the third of the 5-match bilateral ODI series between Afghanistan and Ireland in Noida.
